anomalies.observed: R11, the series element between servo header J4 pin 3 and the bus-select net /NET0021, is valued 1k (LCSC C21190). The netlist has no R9 at all.
anomalies.expected: The spec lists R9-R12 as 0 Ω jumpers. The schematic note reads 'Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others', so R11 should be a 0 Ω jumper that is shorted for non-Core2/CoreS3 builds.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2

anomalies.impact: Ch.1 servo signal reaches its bus GPIO only through a 1 kΩ resistor, not the intended 0 Ω jumper. This adds series impedance and an RC delay on the PWM signal and changes which bus pins are selected for this channel.

anomalies.observed: R4 (0 Ω) ties servo header J4 pin 3 directly to the MAX3485 A line (/NET0020), and R8 (0 Ω) ties J4 pin 3 directly to J8 pin 3. Both 0 Ω links are populated together with the 1 kΩ PWM series resistors R11 and R17, so the serial bus shorts and the PWM GPIO paths are all present at once.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes the two servo interface modes as mutually exclusive. PWM mode uses 1 kΩ series resistors R3/R4 from the PWM nets to the servo pin 3, and serial mode uses the R13/R14 shorts to tie the servo pins to the MAX3485 bus. The spec does not allow both to be populated.

evidence.quote: R3, R4 | 1k each | Series resistors from the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively.
Serial mode (populate R13/R14 ...): J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 are tied together into one shared bus node

anomalies.impact: With the servo signal pins shorted together and also driven from GPIO through 1 kΩ, the GPIO outputs and the MAX3485 driver can contend on the same line. This can corrupt serial-servo communication or the PWM signal, and it defeats the mode separation the spec requires.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows R11 as 1 kΩ where the spec requires a 0 Ω jumper, and R4 and R8 as 0 Ω bridges that appear to populate the serial-mode shorts alongside the PWM series paths. The reference designators differ from the spec, so these findings are moderate-confidence rather than certain.
